nodes.description: Biallelic nonsense, frameshift and start-loss variants remove functional kizuna. Kizuna is a centrosomal protein phosphorylated by PLK1; in dividing cells it keeps the pericentriolar material attached to the centrioles so that the mitotic spindle stays bipolar. Its function in post-mitotic photoreceptors is not known. ClinGen records biallelic loss of function as the mechanism. Patient fibroblasts compound heterozygous for two truncating alleles showed no detectable change in KIZ transcript level, protein localization or cilium length, so the expected loss of protein has not been demonstrated in patient cells.

nodes.description: KIZ is expressed most highly in retina, and the mouse transcript is found in rod photoreceptors of the outer nuclear layer. Mouse PLK1S1 localizes to the base of the rod connecting cilium, and human KIZ to the basal body of primary cilia in fibroblasts. Loss of kizuna is therefore expected to remove a component of the photoreceptor ciliary base; this step rests on localization, not on a demonstrated defect.
